title: Area, centroid, and perimeter of a polygon
prompt: Implement solve(payload), where vertices is an ordered boundary of a simple planar polygon in meters. The boundary may be clockwise or counterclockwise and may repeat its first vertex once at the end. Remove that optional repeated closing vertex from the calculation, without mutating the input. Return {"area_m2":positive_area,"centroid_m":[cx,cy],"perimeter_m":length}. The centroid is the uniform-area centroid, not the average of vertices. Close the last edge to the first. If fewer than three vertices remain, return {"error":"too_few_vertices"}; if the absolute shoelace twice-area is <=1e-12, return {"error":"degenerate"}. Other inputs are valid finite pairs with no self-intersections; zero-area cases are permitted for validation. Absolute/relative tolerance 1e-8.
